RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Senior Backend Engineer | Python and Go
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 21 years of experience building and operating large-scale services in Python, Go and C++. Designed high-throughput services and APIs, including an entitlement service handling 120k requests per second, and contributed to a migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services. Experienced with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, event-driven systems, Kubernetes, observability and automated testing. Fluent in English.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Director of Engineering, Platform - Streamhaus GmbH (video streaming), Munich | 2019 - Aug 2026
- Led the platform organisation responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform; remained hands-on with internal tooling, including cost dashboard scripts.
- Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE; playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Established service templates using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and Terraform modules.
- Built an internal cloud cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports and Looker Studio; rightsizing and committed use discounts reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M/year).
- Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.

Principal Engineer - Streamhaus GmbH | 2015 - 2019
- Technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, Cassandra and Redis.
- Designed and wrote most of the Go entitlement service for subscriptions, regions and devices; handled 120k requests/second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms using Cassandra and local in-memory caching.
- Co-authored the company's service template and Python style guide.

Senior Software Engineer - Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart | 2010 - 2015
- Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
- Led six developers on the route-history product.
- Co-inventor on a granted German patent for adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets.

Software Engineer - Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe | 2005 - 2010
- Developed C++ and Python for industrial data acquisition software on Linux and embedded x86.
- Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Open-source Python retry library | Maintainer, 2012 - 2018
- Maintained a Python retry library with approximately 1,500 GitHub stars; handed over maintenance in 2018.
- Technologies: Python, pytest, tox.

EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc), Computer Science, Rhine Valley University | 2005

SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++ (older experience)
Backend and APIs: FastAPI, Tornado, Django, Flask, asyncio, gRPC, Protobuf
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), Kubernetes, Terraform; AWS (EC2, S3)
Testing and observability: pytest, tox, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management

LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)

PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
- "Running Python at 100k rps" - EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
- "Cost is a feature" - internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with clear reverse-chronological structure, credible scale metrics, and relevant backend engineering achievements. The 120k requests/second entitlement service, 60-service migration, 99.95% availability, and EUR 4.2M annual cloud savings provide strong evidence of impact. The document also presents the candidate's leadership background without obscuring the technical content. The main content weakness is that several bullets describe broad responsibilities or technologies without explicitly connecting them to the target role's Python service development, REST, PostgreSQL ownership, testing, and production operations. The CV also presents a very senior profile for a role advertised at a few years of experience, so the opening should more directly position the candidate as a hands-on backend engineer rather than primarily an engineering leader.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is good: the CV uses standard headings, conventional chronology, readable text, explicit technology names, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It should parse reliably and has strong keyword coverage for Python, Go, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, automated testing, and cloud deployment. AI screening probability is high for the general backend-engineering requirements and medium for this specific vacancy because the document does not explicitly show Docker, REST API design/consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, or substantial AWS deployment experience. These are genuine evidence gaps in the candidate material rather than keywords that should be added speculatively. AWS should be qualified as earlier or limited experience so the document does not imply a depth of AWS experience that the candidate's notes do not support.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with Python/Go backend services, high-throughput APIs, distributed systems, event ingestion, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, automated testing, technical trade-offs, and English communication. The fleet-telematics experience is particularly relevant to Tessel's logistics and tracking domain, and the route-history and GPS-ingestion work should be made more prominent. The candidate exceeds the experience level requested and has credible production-reliability and architecture experience. Gaps include Docker, AWS deployment depth, explicit REST API work, PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, and CI/CD. The source material does not establish experience with these areas, so they should not be added merely to match the advertisement. Dutch or French language skills and EDI formats are also not present. The culture fit is reasonably supported by the RFC process, architecture reviews, on-call guidelines, service ownership, and operational reliability examples.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary section, change the opening to position the candidate more directly for this hands-on role. For example: "Senior backend engineer with 21 years of experience building and operating large-scale services in Python, Go and C++, including high-throughput APIs, event ingestion and distributed systems." Retain the leadership background later in the summary, but make hands-on backend engineering the first message.

2. In the Summary section, replace the broad phrase "Experienced with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, event-driven systems, Kubernetes, observability and automated testing" with a more evidence-based version that connects to the target domain: "Experienced with PostgreSQL/PostGIS-backed fleet-telematics systems, message-driven ingestion, Kubernetes, observability and automated testing." This uses terminology supported by the Nordfels and project information without implying unsupported REST, Docker, CI/CD, query-tuning, or schema-migration experience.

3. In the Senior Software Engineer role at Nordfels Telematik AG, revise the first bullet to foreground the logistics relevance and event-ingestion terminology: "Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ; led backend development for route-history functionality." This makes the transport, tracking, ingestion, relational database, and message-queue alignment easier for both ATS and recruiters to identify.

4. In the Principal Engineer role, revise "Technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, Cassandra and Redis" to include the supported service-design impact: "Technical lead for a high-throughput playback API, using Python, Tornado, Cassandra and Redis, with responsibility for production reliability and performance." Do not label this API as REST unless the candidate can substantiate that it was REST-based.

5. In the Skills section, change "AWS (EC2, S3)" to "AWS (EC2, S3; earlier experience)". This accurately reflects the candidate's notes that AWS exposure was limited and historical, while preserving the supported AWS keywords for ATS parsing.

6. In the Testing and observability skills line, retain "pytest" and "tox" and consider changing the heading to "Testing, CI/CD and observability" only if the document contains substantiated CI/CD experience. Otherwise, leave CI/CD out; the current candidate information supports automated testing but does not support a CI/CD claim.

7. In the Selected Projects section, consider adding the existing Entitlement Service project from the candidate portfolio between the migration and open-source projects. Use only the supported details: "Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service for subscriptions, regions and devices; handled 120k requests/second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms using Cassandra and local in-memory caching. Technologies: Go, gRPC, Cassandra, Redis, Kubernetes." This gives the target role a concise, technically concrete example of production backend ownership.

8. In the Selected Projects section, consider adding the existing Monolith to Services Migration project or incorporate its specific implementation details into the Director role: "Set up service templates using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and Terraform modules." The current CV contains this information, but placing it in a clearly scannable project or achievement bullet would strengthen alignment with FastAPI, observability, Kubernetes/cloud deployment, and infrastructure-as-code requirements.
